answers.core: It would be an integral part of how TileMaps are rendered. I don't think an add-on can hook into this, at the moment, but I'm not sure.
answers.workaround:
One way to work around this is to create tons of materials, each having different shader uniforms. I solved my case by creating 47 different materials in a script. But I think this is inefficient for rendering (no batching), and can lead to combinatorial explosions.

It works fine though, and it might be that in a 2D game the lack of batching for having lots of material variants isn't a significant performance issue. But while implementing I thought of this abstract solution which seems slightly more elegant "why would the shader *not* have access to this".

title: Allow passing per-tile custom data to a shader
